blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines—Influenza-like illness (ILI) remained the most frequently reported among diseases in Manila, with 18 new cases recorded on Monday, bringing the city’s year-to-date total to 1,955, according to the latest W.I.L.D. diseases report covering water-borne diseases, influenza, leptospirosis and dengue. The report, based on data extracted from the Electronic Disease Case Surveillance and Information System (EDCS-IS) as of 7 a.m. on Sept. 28, also recorded 13 new dengue cases, 10 new severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) cases, three new leptospirosis cases and one new typhoid fever case. No new cholera or confirmed COVID-19 cases were recorded on the same day. […]... Keep on reading: 18 new cases of flu-like illness reported in Manila; 1,955 total cases
